newsitem.title: INDIA: India, China initial border agreement.
newsitem.headline: India, China initial border agreement.

text.p: India and China on Friday initialled an agreement to minimise the possibility of armed conflict on their border, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
It gave no details of the agreement, which it said was initialled after official talks between visiting Chinese President Jiang Zemin and Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.

PTI said three other agreements were also initialled -- on preventing illegal drug trafficking, setting up direct shipping links betwen the two countries and maintaining an Indian consulate office in Hong Kong after mid-1997.
"India and China today agreed to take vital confidence building measures to minimise the possibility of any armed conflict at their borders...," the agency said.
The two countries fought a brief Himalayan border war in 1962 and troops are still deployed along both sides of the rugged line of actual control.
India and China signed an agreement in 1993 to ease tension along their 4,000 km (2,500 mile) frontier during a visit by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao to Beijing.
